title: Tilt & Ship KPI scratchpad — 3-week pulse
body:
Purpose: quick working doc to track the next 3-week focus cycle. I want something lightweight I can iterate on — not a formal OKR doc yet.

Context / north star: move small bets towards measurable throughput improvements in my personal productivity: fewer blockers + faster handoffs = 20% more focused deep-work hours per sprint.

Top-level outcome (northstar): +20% deep-focus hours (measured as 90+ min uninterrupted blocks) across a 3-week window.

Draft objectives and candidate key results (raw):
- O1: Increase uninterrupted deep-work blocks
  - KR1: Average deep block length >= 90 min, 3x per week (baseline: 1.6/week)
  - KR2: Reduce daily task-switch events (Slack pings + meetings) by 30%
- O2: Ship two small automation tweaks that reduce manual triage time
  - KR3: Deploy two scripts (triage-bot + sprint-sort) with <15 min manual run time per day saved
  - KR4: Track time-savings using a light spreadsheet and 5 quick time audits
- O3: Improve adoption of personal templating + meeting playbook
  - KR5: <2 meetings/week that run without an agenda or outcome note

Reality check / constraints:
- baseline measurement is messy — need a short measurement plan. simplest: a daily 30s log, tagged: deep-block, interruption, manual-triage, meeting-no-agenda.
- blocking risks: calendar overflow from leadership syncs, surprise ops incidents, family commitments.
- automation dependencies: small infra PRs may require eng review >1 week. scope down to a single feature if needed.

Measurement plan (quick + hacky):
- daily: 30s entry in a single row sheet (date, deep-block-count, longest-block-mins, interrupt-count, manual-triage-mins, meetings-no-agenda)
- weekly: aggregate and quick chart for trend (sheet auto sum), quick note in this doc
- spot-check: 3 randomized time-audits (5–10 min) during week 2 to validate self-reported numbers

Week 0 (setup) checklist — things to do before week 1 starts:
- [ ] Create sheet + template row (linked artifact above)
- [ ] Add short Slack status: "heads-down windows" (2 × 90m blocks, tentative) — ask team to prefer async
- [ ] Draft two minimal automation ideas and open one engineering PR (scope: run locally + cron)
- [ ] Prep meeting agenda template and add to calendar invites

Micro experiments (run and decide):
- A: Calendar gating: set "no-meetings" blocks (90m) at 10:00 and 15:00 for 3 weeks. Hypothesis: >1 usable deep block per day after day 3.
- B: Quick triage script: auto-label incoming flagged items and keep a 10-item review queue. Hypothesis: triage time down by 8–12 min/day after week 1.
- C: One-touch meeting template: 1-line goal + 2 expected outcomes. Hypothesis: reduces runover/extra follow-ups by 30%.

Signals to watch (leading + lagging):
- Leading: proportion of calendar free in targeted windows, time between interruptions, triage queue depth
- Lagging: average deep-block length, number of context switches per day, subjective energy score (end-of-day quick 3pt)

Notes from quick baseline (week before start):
- measured 1–2 deep blocks/week, avg longest-block 60m, interruptions ~7/day, manual triage ~22 min/day, meetings without agenda ~3/week
- initial guess: meaningful improvement if long-blocks increase to 2.5/week and interruptions <5/day

Open questions / unresolved:
- should I try a strict block calendar or a social nudge to the team first? (cost: brief sync vs risk of social friction)
- automation scope: do I own infra PR or get SE help? faster to pair, slower to land if I wait for review
- measurement overhead: is daily logging going to be too heavy and bias behavior? Keep at 30s or use a watch/timer?

Next actions (this doc's short TODO for today):
- [ ] Create the tracking sheet and add a sample row (15m) — target: done today
- [ ] Post a short note in #team-hub about experimental "heads-down" windows and ask for feedback (5m)
- [ ] Sketch the triage script in a notebook and open a WIP PR titled "triage-lite" (30–45m)

Quick retrospective notes (end-of-week template to fill):
- What went well?
- What blocked me?
- One concrete tweak for next week
- Energy score (1–5)

Tone / meta: keep this doc messy and editable. I want a log that reads like a lab notebook — short bullets, fast experiments, quick rejects. If an idea is winning after 2 cycles, promote it to a formal OKR doc and move the measurement into a shared sheet.

Scratch math (how much time to save to hit north star):
- baseline deep-focus blocks: 1.6/week -> target 3/week = +1.4 blocks/week -> ~>126 extra minutes/week (assuming 90min blocks)
- time saved from triage (target 15 min/day) = 75 min/week -> combined with calendar changes could reach the 120–150 min target

Random observations (notes to self):
- shorter check-ins with managers tend to ripple into fewer followups — try 12-min syncs
- automated triage must be conservative — false positives cost more time than manual triage sometimes

References / links (quick):
- personal timing sheet: (placeholder) https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-personal-tilt
- related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/tilt-experiments/pull/78
- related jira: PROJ-4321

End-of-doc: will iterate on this nightly for first week and then consolidate week notes into a short 1-pager for my manager.
